## Overview

The analysis pipeline produces a set of self-contained, interactive HTML
files alongside the static figures. Each file is a standalone web page:
open it in any modern browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) by double-clicking
— no server, internet connection, or additional software is required.
Geometry is rebuilt in the browser from a small block of embedded
coefficients or vectors, so the pages respond live to user controls
(rotation, sliders, toggles).

All interactive files live under `analysis/output/html/`:

```         
analysis/output/html/
├── scar_alignment_svd.html              # SVD alignment diagnostic (4 panels)
├── scar_alignment_lin2024.html          # Lin 2024 alignment diagnostic (3 panels)
├── kde_sphere_interactive/              # scar-direction density on a sphere
│   ├── kde_sphere_EXP.html
│   ├── kde_sphere_IM.html
│   └── kde_sphere_SDG.html
└── reconstruction_interactive/          # SPHARM shape reconstructions
    ├── interactive_EXP.html
    ├── interactive_IM.html
    ├── interactive_SDG.html
    ├── interactive_EXP_CoIA_axes.html
    └── interactive_SDG_CoIA_axes.html
```

Three dataset codes appear throughout the filenames:

- **EXP** — the experimental knapped cores.
- **IM** — the eight idealized digital core models (sourced from Lin et
  al. 2024: cylindrical, conical, discoidal, Levallois, biface, and
  polyhedral types).
- **SDG** — the archaeological Sandinggai core assemblage.

The sections below describe what each file shows and how to read it,
together with the script that generates it.

## Scar-direction alignment diagnostics

These two pages visualise, specimen by specimen, the orientation-
standardisation that is applied to the raw flaking-scar vectors before
any spherical-harmonic analysis. In both pages a **dropdown at the top
selects the specimen**, every panel is a fully rotatable/zoomable 3D
plot, and a short caption beneath each panel states what that step does.
A colour key is printed below the dropdown.

### `scar_alignment_svd.html`

Generated by `analysis/scripts/r_alignment/align_svd.R`. This is the
alignment used for the **main analysis**. It shows the four-step SVD
pipeline as four side-by-side panels:

- **Step 0 — Raw data.** Scar start/end points in their original
  coordinates, with the SVD-fitted best-fit plane and its normal.
- **Step 1 — Rotate.** The best-fit plane normal (the third right
  singular vector of the unit scar-direction vectors) is rotated onto
  the Z-axis, so the plane lies flat in XY.
- **Step 2 — Translate.** The centroid of all scar endpoints is moved to
  the origin, removing positional bias between specimens.
- **Step 3 — Rotate XY.** The dominant in-plane scar direction (first
  singular vector of the XY projections) is rotated onto the X-axis, so
  every specimen shares a common reference frame.

Colour key: blue = flaking scars, red arrow = SVD normal, orange arrow =
PCA main axis (X), grey plane = SVD best-fit plane.

### `scar_alignment_lin2024.html`

Generated by `analysis/scripts/r_alignment/align_lin2024.R`. This page
documents the alternative alignment of Lin et al. 2024, used in the
**rotational-invariance validation** rather than the main pipeline. It
has three panels:

- **Step 0 — Direction vectors / reference normal.** Unit direction
  vectors are computed from scar endpoints; the morphological plane
  normal (`Norm_X/Y/Z`, measured externally in Geomagic) serves as the
  reference orientation.
- **Step 1 — Rotate.** A Rodrigues rotation aligns the measured
  morphological normal with the Z-axis, placing the best-fit plane in
  XY.
- **Step 2 — Translate (Lin 2024).** The longest scar is identified and
  its rotated start-point is moved to (0, 0), anchoring the origin while
  preserving the absolute spatial relationships between scars.

Colour key: blue = flaking scars, pink = longest scar, red arrow = plane
normal, grey plane = best-fit plane.

The contrast with the SVD page is deliberate: this method uses the
*measured* normal (not an SVD-fitted one), anchors the *longest scar*
(not the centroid), and performs *no* in-plane rotation. Viewing the two
pages side by side makes the rotational-invariance argument concrete.

## Scar-direction density on the sphere

### `kde_sphere_interactive/kde_sphere_{EXP,IM,SDG}.html`

Generated by
`analysis/scripts/SPHARM_modules/spherical_kde_interactive_export.py`,
one file per dataset. Each page renders the **von Mises–Fisher kernel
density estimate (KDE) of a specimen's flaking-scar direction vectors on
a single unit sphere**, coloured by density (viridis colour map). This
is the spherical density that the SP-SPHARM descriptors are computed
from, shown here as a directly inspectable surface.

Only the raw direction vectors are embedded; the KDE itself is
recomputed in the browser, so the density responds live to the bandwidth
control.

Controls:

- **Specimen dropdown**, grouped by core type (Typology).
- **Bandwidth slider (`bw`)** — recomputes the KDE on the fly; the
  concentration parameter is *κ = 1/bw²*.
- **Type Mean** — pools the direction vectors of every specimen of the
  selected type and re-fits the KDE, giving a per-type average pattern.
- **Scars** — toggles the scatter of individual scar-direction points
  over the density surface.
- **Contours** — overlays iso-density contour lines (marching squares).
- **2D Map** — an equirectangular density map (bearing 0–360° × plunge
  +90°…−90°).
- **Graticule**, **view presets** (Iso / Top / Front), **material**
  selector, **Info** panel, a density **colour bar**, and **PNG**
  export.

How to read it: tight, bright hot-spots indicate strongly clustered
(anisotropic) scar directions; a diffuse, even colouring indicates
near-isotropic scarring.

## SPHARM shape reconstructions

### `reconstruction_interactive/interactive_{EXP,IM,SDG}.html`

Generated by
`analysis/scripts/SPHARM_modules/spharm_interactive_export.py`, one file
per dataset. Each page is a **dual viewport**: the **Morphology**
reconstruction (M-SPHARM, left) and the **Scar-direction field**
reconstruction (SP-SPHARM, right) for the same specimen, with
synchronised rotation and zoom. The surfaces are synthesised in the
browser in real time from the stored spherical-harmonic coefficients (up
to degree *l* = 20).

Controls:

- **Specimen dropdown**, grouped by core type.
- **Degree slider (`l ≤`)** with a **play button** — rebuilds the
  surface using only harmonics up to the chosen degree, and animates *l*
  = 1 → 20 to show how detail accumulates as higher frequencies are
  added.
- **Type Mean** — averages the coefficients across all specimens of the
  selected type and reconstructs that mean shape.
- **Colormap** — shades the surface by radial deviation from its mean
  radius (blue = inward, red = outward), with a colour bar.
- **Wire** (wireframe), **material** selector, **view presets**,
  **Info** panel, plus **PNG** screenshot and **OBJ** mesh export.

How to read it: comparing the two viewports shows how a specimen's
external shape (left) relates to its scar-direction organisation
(right); the degree slider illustrates the level of harmonic detail that
the descriptors retain.

### `reconstruction_interactive/interactive_{EXP,SDG}_CoIA_axes.html`

Generated by the `export_axis_interactive_html()` routine in
`analysis/scripts/SPHARM_modules/spharm_reconstruction.py` (reusing the
viewer above). These pages exist only for the two real datasets that
have a co-inertia analysis (CoIA): **EXP** and **SDG**.

Instead of individual specimens, the dropdown steps through **synthetic
average shapes sampled along the CoIA axes** that summarise the
covariation between the morphology block and the scar-direction block.
For each of *Morph Axis 1/2* and *Scar Axis 1/2*, the axis is sampled at
a sequence of positions (across a robust percentile range); at each
position a Gaussian-kernel-weighted mean of the coefficients is
reconstructed. The Info panel reports the axis, the axis coordinate of
the current step, the kernel bandwidth, and the effective sample size
behind each averaged shape.

How to read it: stepping along an axis animates the shape (and/or
scar-pattern) change that the axis captures — i.e. a visual rendering of
the morphological and directional gradients identified by the CoIA,
which the static figures summarise only as arrows or loadings.

## Reproducing the files

The two alignment diagnostics are produced as part of the `targets`
pipeline (the `align_svd_csvs` and `align_lin2024_csv` targets). The KDE
and reconstruction pages are produced by running the standalone scripts
named above inside the project Docker image. All outputs are written to
`analysis/output/html/`, which is git-ignored, so they are regenerated
locally rather than committed.
